_comment: Channel topology for the CCV core, from the block-level grill-me
(2026-09-23). Every channel is one port on each of two blocks, so this
list IS the design's connectivity and the per-block port index is a
lookup into it rather than a second source.
WHAT IS HERE AND WHAT IS NOT. The topology -- which blocks, which
direction, what rate, what fields -- is complete and checked. Field
WIDTHS are not: most firm up in the per-block session that owns the
interface, and inventing them here would put a number in the generated
typedef that nobody decided. So payload structs are generated only for
channels whose widths are settled; the rest generate topology alone.
COMMON PORTS are not channels and are not listed here -- see
common_ports below. Every block declares them, generated rather than
COUNTS. 40 channels. The source spec's prose says 32 and its per-block
port index runs low on 7 of 14 blocks; the enumerated tables are
self-consistent and are what this file follows. tools/gen-interfaces.py
derives the per-block counts from the channel list so the two can never

common_ports.name: clk_free
common_ports.doc: Ungated clock, for the wake detector ONLY. Anything else on it defeats the block's gate invisibly (CCV-L22).

common_ports.name: rst_n
common_ports.doc: Synchronous reset, ACTIVE LOW. `CCV_RST is the in-reset condition, so a block spells it `!rst_n`.

common_ports.name: kill_valid
common_ports.doc: Grid teardown, one cycle ahead of the mask. Outside the credit scheme: a kill must not wait on a stalled receiver.

common_ports.name: kill_warp_mask
common_ports.doc: Warps to discard, from RAU. Grid ID appears on no interface -- RAU converts it from its warp-to-CTA-to-grid tables, so every receiver just masks warp-indexed state.

common_ports.name: wake_req
common_ports.doc: Ungate request from any peer. Outside the credit scheme.

common_ports.name: sleep_ok
common_ports.doc: Block is drained and may be gated.

common_ports.name: csr_credit
common_ports.doc: Credit return for the CSR channel.

channel_signals.doc: Asserted ONE CYCLE AHEAD of the payload, on every interface without exception. A credit is consumed when valid asserts, not when the payload lands, and once asserted valid is binding -- the payload follows on schedule even if a stall arrives in between.
The packed struct. Same flop count as valid, so it arrives no later than it otherwise would.
Stall-invalidate: temporarily invalidates outstanding credits. No message may be sent the cycle after it is received, which makes the in-flight window a fixed count rather than a handshake.

channels.name: ccv_rcu_lane_ops
channels.note: Fans out to 32 LANE instances; the payload is per-lane.

channels.name: ccv_miu_ooe_cmpl
channels.note: One struct covering completion and faults together; miss notification rides the same path and is the primary demotion trigger.

channels.name: ccv_mlc_dcu_probe
channels.note: A wake source: the D-cache cannot sleep through an inbound probe.

channels.name: ccv_exb_ext
channels.note: THE ONE EXCEPTION. TileLink TL-C at the coherent boundary; obeys that protocol's rules, not ours. Containing it in a bridge block is what keeps the exception to a single port.

_field_widths_comment: Payload field -> width, as a SystemVerilog expression over ccv_params_pkg
and ccv_prov_pkg. A field absent from this map has no decided width, so
its channel generates a field LIST rather than a packed struct, and
Inventing the missing ones here would put a number nobody decided into a
generated typedef, and generated numbers get believed. They are enumerated
instead, so the ask to each per-block session is a specific short list.
_open_fields_comment: The payload fields with NO decided width, and the specific question each
per-block session has to answer. A question rather than a placeholder on
purpose: a placeholder width would reach a generated typedef and be
believed, whereas an unanswered question blocks loudly.
`owner` names the blocks on the channels, which is who has to answer.
`flag` marks the ones where independent per-block answers would collide.

asid.question: Address-space id width, i.e. how many address spaces are concurrently resident before an ASID rollover / TLB flush is required. Appears on both translation channels and on the launch channel, so it is the same field in all three; one number.
asid.flag: Only open field here that is clearly ONE encoding across its channels.

bank_select.question: Which register bank a migration targets on ccv_rau_rcu_mig. Needs the banking factor of the PRF, which has not been stated anywhere yet.

byte_mask.question: Write byte-enables on ccv_miu_spm_req. Almost certainly write_data/8, but write_data's own width is set by the SPM word size (CCV_W_SPM_WORD = 10 addresses 32-bit words), so confirm the beat width rather than assuming.

class.question: How many uop classes, and is class a strict partition of opcode space (so class is derivable from opcode and is carried only to save decode) or an orthogonal attribute? The answer sets whether this field is load-bearing or an optimisation.

code_bounds.question: Code region bounds on launch. Two questions: is this a base+limit pair or a base+size, and is it at page granularity (narrowing it considerably) or byte granularity at CCV_W_VA?

conflict_serialization.question: Reported bank-conflict serialisation on ccv_spm_miu_rsp. Is this a count of extra cycles taken (width = log2 of worst-case serialisation, bounded by 32 banks) or a per-lane conflict bitmap? A count is cheap and enough for the timing model; a bitmap is what a debug trace would want.

cta_id.question: CTA identifier on the fault channel. Distinct from the decided CCV_P_W_CTA_SLOT (3 bits, a hardware slot index): this looks like the software-visible CTA id from the launch grid, which is much wider. Confirm which is meant -- if it is the slot, reuse CCV_P_W_CTA_SLOT and rename the field.

data.question: Read-return data on ccv_dcu_miu_rsp. Named `data` while the SPM path names the same concept `read_data` / `write_data` -- worth unifying. Width is the DCU beat, which needs stating: full line, or CCV_W_DATA, or a narrower beat with multiple transfers.

demotion_threshold.question: Tier-1 demotion threshold, a CSR-programmed policy value. Width is a policy range decision, not an architectural one: state the units (cycles? retired instructions? MLC misses?) and the range worth expressing.

index_per_lane.question: Per-lane index for a gather/scatter on ccv_rcu_miu_addr. Two numbers needed: the index width per lane, and whether all 32 lanes ship per beat or a subset. At 32 lanes x a 32-bit index this is a 1024-bit field, so if that is not intended the channel needs a narrower index or more beats.

itlb_refill.question: The only field on ccv_miu_fet_itlb, so it is the whole payload: a translation result. Needs the iTLB entry format -- PPN (CCV_P_W_PA minus page offset) plus permissions plus whatever the refill FSM requires.

launch_block_addr.question: Address of the CTA launch block in memory. Presumably CCV_W_VA or CCV_P_W_PA -- state which side of translation this is on, since the channel goes to the MIU.

op.owner: memory hierarchy (miu, spm, dcu, mlc, exb)
op.question: Is this ONE encoding or three? It appears on five channels at three different levels: ccv_ooe_miu_memop (architectural memory op), ccv_miu_spm_req (scratchpad bank access), and ccv_miu_dcu_req / ccv_dcu_mlc_req / ccv_mlc_exb_req (cache-line request, where it must also carry coherence intent). A scratchpad bank has no notion of ownership and a cache line has no notion of a lane-strided access, so one shared encoding across all five looks unlikely. Decide whether to keep one field name with three widths or rename them apart; then give the operation list at each level.
op.flag: Widest blast radius of any open field, and the one most likely to be wrong if each session decides alone.

opcode.question: Same question, one level down: dec->ooe carries a decoded uop opcode, ooe->rcu carries what the scheduler issues, and rcu->lane carries what a lane actually executes. Is this one encoding narrowing along the pipe, or re-encoded at each hop? If it narrows, the width is set once by the widest (dec->ooe); if it re-encodes, three numbers. Note dec->ooe already carries a separate `class` field, so the split between class and opcode needs stating either way.

operand.question: One operand's worth of data on ccv_rcu_lane_ops -- but the channel is per-lane at rate 4, so state whether this is one lane's element (CCV_W_LANE_DATA), a full row (CCV_W_DATA), or a bundle of N source operands. The rate and the width together set the wire cost of the whole execute path, so this one is worth getting right before floorplan.

ordering.question: Memory ordering / fence semantics carried per op. Enumerate the orderings the ISA exposes (relaxed, acquire, release, acq_rel, seq_cst?) and whether scope (CTA / core / system) is encoded in the same field or separately.

ownership_class.question: Coherence ownership class on ccv_mlc_exb_req. Enumerate the states requested at this boundary (the MESI/MOESI subset actually used); the width falls out. Related to `op` on the same channel, so decide the two together -- ownership intent may belong inside op.

pcs.question: PLURAL, and that is the question: how many PCs travel in one migration? SMT-4 tier-1 suggests four, but the channel moves a whole parked context, so it may be one PC per warp in the migrating group, or one per divergence-stack entry. State what the set is over, then the count follows CCV_W_VA times that.

pred_state.question: Predicate/divergence state for a migrating context. Needs the divergence representation first: a reconvergence stack of N entries (depth x (mask + PC)) or a flat per-lane mask set. This is the field most likely to be underestimated, because it is where the divergence model is actually stored.

prf_base.question: Physical register file base for a warp's allocated window. Follows CCV_P_PHYS_REGS (CCV_P_W_PHYS_REG = 8 provisional), but confirm whether allocation is at register granularity or in fixed-size chunks -- chunked allocation narrows both this and prf_size.

prf_size.question: Size of that window. Same granularity question as prf_base; the two are one decision.

progress_threshold.question: Companion to demotion_threshold and the same decision: units and range. Both are tuning knobs, so they may reasonably be the widest thing a CSR write can carry rather than a tight fit.

retired_since_restore.question: Retire count since context restore, feeding the progress/demotion policy. Width is a saturation choice: pick the count at which the policy stops caring and saturate there, rather than sizing for a true maximum.

size.question: Access size at the cache level, on ccv_miu_dcu_req and ccv_mlc_exb_req. Distinct from the decided CCV_W_CHWIDTH (element width code, 2 bits) which lives at the architectural level. Give the legal transfer sizes -- if they are powers of two up to a line, this is a small code rather than a byte count.

space.question: Memory space selector (global / shared / scratchpad / const / local?). Enumerate the spaces; the width is ceil(log2(count)) unless a one-hot is wanted for decode speed.

status.question: Completion status on ccv_miu_ooe_cmpl. The channel already carries a separate `cause` field (CCV_W_FAULT_CAUSE) and `mlc_miss`, so state what status adds beyond ok/fault -- if it is only ok/fault it is 1 bit and cause carries the rest.

sub_width.question: How a lane subdivides its 32-bit datapath for packed SIMD. If the legal set is exactly CCV_W_CHWIDTH's (32/16/8/4) then this is that code and should say so rather than being a second field; if lanes support something chwidth cannot express, state what.

tilelink_tlc.question: The only external-facing channel. This is a whole TileLink TL-C bundle, not a scalar: decide the TileLink parameters (beat width, source/sink id widths, address width) and whether this channel carries the flattened bundle or is decomposed into the five TL channels. Until then it cannot be given a single width.
tilelink_tlc.flag: Not a field width so much as an external protocol binding.
